primary_question: Does a preregistered longitudinal multimodal model improve held-out calibration and proper scoring for sustained cessation of longitudinal bone growth beyond chronological age and bone age?

hypotheses.statement: MRI growth-plate and puberty-related feature blocks improve primary held-out calibration and Brier score beyond the baseline.
hypotheses.falsifier: No repeatable improvement or failed calibration.

hypotheses.statement: The model retains acceptable calibration across registered sites and developmental subgroups.
hypotheses.falsifier: Subgroup calibration or external-site transportability gate fails.

hypotheses.statement: Inherited feature summaries do not need to be retained if they add no stable predictive value after ancestry-aware controls.
hypotheses.falsifier: No incremental performance, or unfairness/instability is detected.

population.age_range: prepubertal through late-pubertal windows fixed before enrollment
population.sample_size: set by preregistered simulation; no sample-size claim is made in this proposal

endpoints.primary: sustained low-growth state based on registered height-velocity threshold across two consecutive follow-up intervals
endpoints.secondary: interval-censored MRI structural growth-plate closure; residual height gain; uncertainty interval calibration
non_endpoints: causal effect of a hormone or genotype

feature_blocks: bone age if approved and available

leakage_controls: fit preprocessing and feature selection in training only
keep repeated visits within participant-aware splits

ethics_and_governance: no research biopsy or hormone manipulation
separate genomic consent and withdrawal process
human specialist review before any interpretation
stop_conditions: endpoint misclassification too high for a defensible analysis
subgroup sample support inadequate for declared fairness claims
